taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-02, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 31374.7 | 20.07 | 20.07
2 | 7559.9 | 12.79 | 32.86
3 | 3573.3 | 1.62 | 34.48
4 | 313.2 | 38.90 | 73.38
5 | 53.6 | 0.41 | 73.79
6 | 22.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as Q-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-02, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station T-02, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation at T-02 resolves a six-layer resistivity sequence. Resistivity decreases steadily with depth: Layer 1 (31,374.7 Ω·m, 0–20.07 m), Layer 2 (7,559.9 Ω·m, to 32.86 m), Layer 3 (3,573.3 Ω·m, to 34.48 m), Layer 4 (313.2 Ω·m, to 73.38 m), Layer 5 (53.6 Ω·m, to 73.79 m), and Layer 6 (22.8 Ω·m, basal layer, undifferentiated thickness).

Applying the curve-type notation to each consecutive triplet (r1>r2>r3 in every case) yields Q-Q-Q-Q, consistent with a uniform Q-type descending resistivity curve. This matches the filed classification for this station. The monotonic decrease suggests a resistive near-surface unit (likely dry/compact material) grading into progressively more conductive layers at depth, possibly indicating increasing moisture content, clay content, or weathering with depth. No anomalies or inversions in the resistivity trend were observed.

{"curve_type_stated": "Q", "label_issue_flagged": false}
